name: Moldova

findings.summary: Huawei won state operator Moldtelecom's May 2009 3G equipment tender, reportedly at about half rivals' cost; Bank of China loans and Huawei supplier credits financed the 3G equipment and post-warranty services.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 3: tender award plus financed equipment supply. Two opened S3 sources but no S1/S2, so not corroborated. AidData records two 2010 BOC loans (78.8m and 67.8m lei) and BOC+Huawei lending of 236.8m lei by end-2010; not converted to a contract value because loans may cover more than this award. IPN page undated; events dated from text (tender 14 May 2009). Pre-2020 and still_current unverified: whether Huawei still supplies Moldtelecom's radio/core (4G/5G) is unknown.

findings.summary: Ericsson Nikola Tesla disclosed to the Zagreb Stock Exchange a contract worth almost HRK 56 million with Tiraspol-based operator Interdnestrcom for a 4G/LTE network build, related services and software upgrades.

sources.publisher: Zagreb Stock Exchange (Ericsson Nikola Tesla issuer announcement)
Zagreb Stock Exchange (Ericsson Nikola Tesla issuer announcement)

findings.analyst_inference: Both ZSE notices show publication '09/03/2016' (day/month order ambiguous), so date coded as 2016. Evertiq (2008) covers an earlier, smaller Ericsson deal with the same operator (about EUR 600k, AXE modernisation), showing a longer relationship but not corroborating the 2016 contract. HRK value not converted. Transnistria is outside Chisinau's control, hence subnational; vendor for the Moldovan-controlled operators Orange Moldova and Moldcell not established. Pre-2020; still_current unverified.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Internal Affairs, Information Technology Service (Traffic Monitoring and Control Center)
findings.builder: Hebei Jianshe Construction Group Co., Ltd
findings.summary: A China-grant-funded contract signed with Hebei Jianshe for the first stage of Moldova's national automated road-traffic surveillance system, covering 47 Chisinau intersections and national roads and using Huawei technology; a further roughly US$10m Chinese grant was later negotiated.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc because Huawei technology is reported as the system basis; operator is the Interior Ministry. IPN article (undated, apparently autumn 2015) confirms cameras operating and a US$10m extension grant under negotiation, not concluded; AidData title (unopened) mentions an RMB 30m grant. No S1/S2, so not corroborated. Pre-2020; still_current unverified.

findings.local_actor: Moldovan police, Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, National Bank, Central Election Commission, prison administration
findings.summary: RFE/RL's review of Moldova's procurement portal found over 7,210 Hikvision and Dahua cameras bought by state bodies in 2018-2023, including police, a Defence Ministry air regiment, the National Bank, prisons and the election commission.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded S4 because RFE/RL is US-government funded (state-affiliated under SPEC); a reviewer may regrade to S3. Underlying data is the public procurement portal, not opened here. Tier 3 for procurement awards; many cameras are presumably operating but no system-level integration was documented. Finding date is the end of the procurement window; article date not captured. No removal decision found.

findings.controller: STISC (Information Technology and Cyber Security Service, state)
findings.local_actor: Agency for Electronic Governance; Ministry of Finance; Ministry of Internal Affairs IT service; Public Service Agency
findings.summary: A 2026 draft government decision continues consolidating public-sector data centres into MCloud, the state-run common government platform operated by STISC, letting three agencies buy interim hardware until end-2028 before handing it to STISC.

sources.publisher: Government of the Republic of Moldova

findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator is a Moldovan state body, so domestic. No foreign vendor, builder or financier named; underlying server/storage vendors unknown. Tier 4 chosen conservatively: platform is operating (consolidation under way since Decisions 414/2018 and 823/2020) but migration is incomplete. Both sources are government, so not corroborated; still_current true from the 2026 draft and a 2024 MCloud decommissioning entry.
